citation.title: Initial operation of the NSTX-Upgrade real-time velocity diagnostic
citation.authors: M Podestà and R E Bell

topic: Real-time C VI charge-exchange spectroscopy (RTV) on NSTX-U providing carbon toroidal velocity, with carbon temperature (TC) available from the same fits, for rotation control.
own_question: Can a dedicated fast CES system deliver carbon velocity and temperature in real time to the plasma control system, and what can its fast data reveal?
actual_method_and_evidence: Four active/background chord pairs viewing the C VI 5290.5 Å line, sampled at up to 5 kHz. The paper compares a simplified real-time Gaussian fit with post-discharge analysis and with standard 0.1 kHz CHERS on a few NSTX-U discharges. vφ and TC agree with CHERS at the nearest CHERS radius; RTV carbon density (nC) disagreed by up to about ±50%. Real-time fits show larger uncertainties. Direct background views are needed: neglecting background distorts results by more than a factor of 2, and second-NB-line injection contaminates the background views. vφ is routed to the PCS as analog signals, but no control algorithm had been implemented yet. Example studies cover sawteeth, magnetic braking, MHD modes and a locked mode.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Dedicated hardware has been built on another device (NSTX-U) to obtain carbon-impurity CES velocity and temperature at sub-ms sampling, with a real-time velocity output to the control system; real-time fits were less certain than offline analysis.
claim_checks.qualification: This is impurity (C VI), not main-ion, temperature. Control was not demonstrated. TC was computed in real time, but only vφ was described as routed to the PCS.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: CES accuracy depends on background separation and beam geometry; standard CES sampling (0.1 kHz there) can miss fast events such as sawteeth.
claim_checks.qualification: These are NSTX-U-specific findings; the CES rate there is not KSTAR's.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs were CES spectra at frame rates of 0.5-5 kHz. No nowcasting or forecasting was performed, and report latency to the PCS was not quantified.
validation_if_relevant: Comparison against CHERS and offline analysis on a few discharges. There was no held-out design.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite as demonstrating rotation or temperature control.
Do not treat the RTV outputs as independent physical truth.
Do not apply the reported rates or noise levels to KSTAR.
Do not use as evidence about main-ion Ti or the value of BES/ECEI information.
Do not imply that our approach is needed because faster hardware is impossible; this paper shows faster upstream measurement is one alternative.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as a hardware/upstream alternative: faster CES acquisition and real-time spectral fitting address the latency problem directly, which frames our downstream nowcast as complementary rather than unique. Also useful for background-subtraction caveats about what CES labels represent.
